name: MAX98357A I2S class-D amplifier
description: Analog Devices (Maxim) MAX98357A mono class-D speaker amplifier with a digital I2S input: no DAC or MCLK needed, 16/24/32-bit audio at 8, 16, 32-48 or 96 kHz, up to 3.2 W into 4 Ω at 5 V, pin-selected gain 3-15 dB (9 dB with GAIN open). SD selects shutdown / left / right / (L+R)/2. Runs on 2.5-5.5 V; logic inputs accept 3.3 V. Sold as: Adafruit I2S 3W Class D Amplifier Breakout - MAX98357A (product 3006), 7-pin header (pad 1-7 per Adafruit's board file) Vin, GND, SD, GAIN, DIN, BCLK, LRC plus a 2-pin speaker terminal block.
eli5: Takes digital sound from your board and drives a small speaker loud enough to hear across a room.

pins.name: Vin
pins.description: Amplifier supply 2.5-5.5 V; 5 V for full power, up to about 650 mA into 4 Ω

pins.name: GND
pins.description: Ground (common with the microcontroller and the speaker supply)

pins.name: SD
pins.description: SD_MODE shutdown / channel select; 1 M pull-up to Vin on the board (with the chip's 100 k pull-down: (L+R)/2). GND = shutdown, > 1.4 V = left only

pins.name: GAIN
pins.description: Gain select: open = 9 dB, GND = 12 dB, 100 k to GND = 15 dB, Vin = 6 dB, 100 k to Vin = 3 dB (read at power-up)

pins.name: DIN
pins.description: I2S serial audio data in (3.3-5 V logic, VIH 1.3 V)

pins.name: BCLK
pins.description: I2S bit clock, 32, 48 or 64 x the sample rate

pins.name: LRC
pins.description: I2S word select / left-right clock (LRCLK): low = left channel, high = right

supplierQuery: Adafruit 3006 MAX98357A I2S class D amplifier breakout
buildNotes: Speaker (4 Ω or more) goes on the + / - terminal block. The outputs are bridge-tied: never connect either speaker wire to GND.
Feed Vin from a 5 V supply that can deliver 800 mA (Adafruit's advice); join its GND to the microcontroller's GND.
Use a sample rate of 8, 16, 32-48 or 96 kHz; 22.05 kHz is outside the chip's LRCLK ranges. BCLK must be 32, 48 or 64 x LRCLK (16-bit stereo gives 32x).
Leave SD open for (L+R)/2 mono; pull it to GND (e.g. a GPIO driven low) to shut the amp down (about 0.6 µA). Send the same sample on both channels so any SD setting plays it.
On a Raspberry Pi Pico, LRC (ws) must be on the GPIO right after BCLK (sck).

example.code:
from machine import I2S, Pin
import math, struct, time

RATE = 16000   # MAX98357A accepts 8, 16, 32-48 or 96 kHz (not 22.05 kHz)
FREQ = 1000    # 16 samples per cycle at 16 kHz
audio = I2S(0, sck=Pin({BCLK}), ws=Pin({LRC}), sd=Pin({DIN}), mode=I2S.TX,
            bits=16, format=I2S.STEREO, rate=RATE, ibuf=8000)

# 10 whole cycles, same sample on left and right so any SD channel setting plays it
n = RATE // FREQ * 10
buf = bytearray(n * 4)
for i in range(n):
    s = int(6000 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * FREQ * i / RATE))
    struct.pack_into('<hh', buf, i * 4, s, s)

time.sleep(1)
print('tone 1000 Hz')
t0 = time.ticks_ms()
while time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) < 2000:
    audio.write(buf)
audio.deinit()
print('stopped')
while True:
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Plays a 1 kHz tone for two seconds, then goes quiet
